title: The Austronesian settlement of Madagascar, c. 500–1000
summary: Madagascar was settled across the Indian Ocean from Borneo, some 7,000 km away. The Malagasy language is closest to Maʼanyan, a language of southeast Borneo. When is contested: early books gave about 400, the loanwords point to the 7th century at the earliest, the oldest sure human presence on the island is about 490, and genes date the Austronesian ancestry to about 1,000 years ago. The crossing was drawn direct from Java; a route through the Maldives is also proposed.

legs.source: Settlement of Madagascar (Wikipedia): the language is closest to Maʼanyan, the crossing proposed direct from Java or by the Maldives
legs.note: drawn as the direct run from Java on the winds and currents; the Maldives route is the rival

events.label: Southeast Borneo, the homeland of the language
events.text: Malagasy descends from the Southeast Barito languages of South Kalimantan, and Maʼanyan is its closest relative. Malay and Javanese traders are said to have brought Maʼanyan people along as labourers, in the first centuries of the Christian era.

events.label: Northern Madagascar, the first landfall
events.text: Dates differ with the method. Early books gave about 400 (Marre and Dahl); some archaeologists place arrival at the start of the era or up to 300 years before, on cut-marked bones, though one such date may be skewed by old carbon; the loanwords point to the 7th century at the earliest (Adelaar); the first unambiguous continuous human presence, at Andavakoera, is about 490; and the genes of the Malagasy give an Austronesian migration of about 1,000 years ago.

events.label: Mahilaka, Ampasindava Bay
events.text: A walled town on the northwest coast, urban from about 1000, in date and plan like the Swahili towns of Kilwa and Manda, making stone bowls and glass beads and trading across the western Indian Ocean. Settlement had by then spread far from the first landfall.
